Singapore: FAIL for the characters themselves. Judged against CONCEPT-01 (docs/concepts/singapore-on-foot.png): a heritage street with mostly Chinese-Singaporean pedestrians in modern casual wear, and a packed hawker hall.

What fails:
- Every civilian shares one male face and body with Western features, with only the skin tone swapped. No East Asian majority reads, and there are no Malay or Indian dress cues such as tudung, baju kurung or sari.
- Women read as men with a hair card and a skirt shell (people_group_close.png, A_live01_chest_2m5.png).
- The Raffles Place crowd does not read as CBD office workers. The only nod is one batik shirt with a lanyard badge (D_live02_chest_2m5.png).
- The hawker hall, the SG-02 situation, has about 2 occupied tables out of more than 30 visible at late afternoon (/private/tmp/opus55/critic/characters-T1/play/cap/E_hawker_still.png).

What works: sun umbrellas, floral and batik shirts, kopi cups, shopping bags and mixed skin tones are plausible local touches. The shophouses, five-foot-way tiles, MBS skyline and stall signs (KAYA TOAST, TEA & COFFEE, RICE & CURRY) carry the sense of Singapore, not the people. - No render was refused by the gate. My scenario waited about 13 min in the opus55 render queue, then ran.. Judge: The better image wins all four pairs clearly: pair 1 A, pairs 2–4 B. None of the four is close. The losing images often hold up on lighting: the golden-hour backlight, dappled shade and long soft shadows are actually attractive. In pairs 2–4 they also have more people on screen than the winners. But all four lose for the same reason: the characters do not look real. The losing frames share these faults: waxy, even skin with no pores or shine; generic painted-looking faces and dull eyes; hair that sits as a solid shell or wig; stiff, near-default poses and claw-like hands; clothing with no folds; and denim or trousers covered in speckle noise. Some faces near the camera are smeared or melted. Their crowds mostly walk the same way and never interact, and their backdrops are vague (pure black shopfronts, bleached untextured towers). They also lack story props and anything that separates the main person from the background. The winners pair detailed faces and clothing with props, setting and composition that tell a story. Fixing character quality (faces, eyes, hair, clothing folds and fabric, natural poses) would do the most good. Varied crowd behaviour comes second. Only pair 1 A (the burning-truck frame) and pair 4 B (the neon boulevard) impressed me; none of the losing images did.
